name: 欧美休闲卡通（4~5头）-纯文本版
description: 直接搭配用户内容使用
scene: 直接搭配用户内容使用
prefix:
STYLE-CORE: polished casual mobile game key art illustration, a 2D painting that imitates a soft 3D render (Pixar-adjacent rendered concept art), clean casual-game rendering with simplified shading and tidy colour masses, high level of finish with every surface fully rendered, soft glossy highlights on every surface, smooth creamy tonal gradients, clean polished game-art finish, no flat areas left unrendered, clean stylised rendering with simplified tidy colour masses, every form built from a small number of large readable shapes rather than accumulated small detail: each material reads as one or two broad colour masses with geometric simplified edges and no micro texture on any surface, surfaces stay smooth and uninterrupted so shapes read as solid blocks of colour and value, soft volumetric gradient shading with ambient occlusion darkening every crease and seam, real volumetric depth and perspective recession with soft cast shadows computed from the geometry, no cel shading and no airbrush haze, forms are solid and read clearly with no drawn outline anywhere: every edge between two colour masses carries a slightly darker seam, a value step or a change of material instead of a drawn line, smooth opaque surfaces with material distinction between cloth, metal, glass, wood, stone and skin stated in broad simple terms, material texture indicated by one or two simple shapes rather than rendered wear and grain.
[CONTENT]
suffix:
[PROPORTION] casual-game cartoon proportions, stylised rather than realistic, but NOT a chibi build: the head reads a little larger than life and modestly enlarged relative to the body, though never an oversized chibi or toy-figure head, about four and a half to five heads tall in total, compact torso, limbs a little shorter than realistic with rounded chunky hands and feet, simplified rounded anatomy with no visible muscle definition, and simple stylised facial features that stay round and simplified. The face stays stylised, not a realistic rendered face
[KEY LIGHT] one clear dominant light source, placed off to one side of the subject and above it, so the light arrives from one definite direction and the far side of every form falls away from it, the light is warm relative to the shadow and the shadow cool relative to the light, brightness decreases steadily the further a surface sits from that source and decays smoothly across the frame, the lit zone holds open mid-tones that stay readable rather than washing out, the shadow side stays deep but never crushes to solid black, every cast shadow is computed from the geometry of the object that throws it and lands in the direction that source demands, exposure is balanced so that nothing clips to pure white and nothing collapses into a black hole
[PALETTE] the whole frame is carried by three to five dominant hues in total, each large mass kept as one broad simple colour, held low in saturation so the picture stays restrained across every large area, with no more than one small high-saturation accent reserved for the focal point, and a full value range present from near-black shadow through the mid-tones up to bright lit faces so no part of the frame is left in one narrow band of brightness
